data.name: Band of Drones
data.detailed_description:
Band of Drones keeps the basic mechanics of traditional turn based squad tactics gameplay and goes beyond it with character and weapons development.

Join the fight for the underground riches of planet Crixius! The Zentris have already placed their drones around several locations, you need to infiltrate their outposts and kick them out of there!

Features

  • Manage a squad of 12 drones, each with their own set of class specifications and powers
  • Evolve your drones along your campaign, upgrading to their powers and weapon handling capabilities
  • Select a squad of 6 drones before each battle
  • Drones gain experience points for upgrades, according to their performance in battle
  • Purchase new weapons and upgrade the ones you have, from a selection of cannons, missile launchers and laser guns
  • Purchase mods for your weapons to improve their performance
  • Different mission goals such as Purge and Withdraw, Assassination, Object Recovery, Destroy Structure, Protect Structure
  • Up to 4 player local co-op mayhem
  • Play in skirmish or story based campaigns over 4 scenarios

reviews.review:
Band of Drones is a turn-based tactical strategy game built around commanding a customizable collection of combat drones on the hostile planet Crixius. Developed and published by Kiritsu Games, it takes a relatively focused approach to squad tactics, emphasizing preparation, positioning, equipment, and gradual unit development instead of elaborate storytelling. The premise involves confronting the occupying Zentris and fighting over strategically important locations and resources. While the narrative provides a reason for the battles, the game's main appeal lies in assembling an effective mechanical squad and deciding how to use its different capabilities.

The roster system provides much of the strategic foundation. Players can maintain a squad of up to twelve drones, but only six can be selected for deployment in a battle. This restriction makes preparation an important part of each engagement because simply collecting powerful units is not enough. Players must consider which combination is most appropriate for the objective ahead. Drones feature different class specifications and abilities, giving them particular battlefield purposes and encouraging a balanced force. As the roster expands, deciding which machines should remain in reserve and which should enter combat becomes an increasingly meaningful part of the strategy.

Individual drones also improve through experience earned according to their battlefield performance. This progression creates continuity between missions and gives successful units greater long-term importance. Abilities and weapon-handling skills can be improved as the campaign progresses, allowing previously modest drones to become increasingly useful. It is a straightforward development system rather than an exceptionally deep role-playing structure, but it complements the tactical gameplay effectively. Keeping experienced units alive and using them intelligently becomes valuable because their accumulated improvements can influence later encounters.

Equipment adds another layer of customization. Players can acquire several types of weapons, including cannons, missile launchers, and laser guns, while existing equipment can be upgraded and modified. These choices allow the squad to be adjusted around different tactical preferences. A player might favor direct firepower and aggressive engagements, while another configuration may emphasize specialized weapons suited to particular targets or situations. The ability to improve both drones and their equipment prevents progression from feeling entirely dependent on simple statistical increases and gives earned resources a practical purpose.

Mission objectives introduce welcome variety to the combat. The available assignments include assassination, recovering objects, destroying structures, defending structures, and Purge and Withdraw operations. Different objectives can alter the player's priorities considerably. Protecting a location encourages defensive positioning and careful control of enemy approaches, while assassination missions can reward concentrated attacks against a particular target. Recovery missions place greater importance on movement, and structure-destruction objectives encourage an offensive approach. This variety helps the relatively simple tactical framework avoid becoming entirely repetitive.

The game includes campaign-oriented play alongside skirmishes spread across four scenarios. The campaign is the better option for experiencing progression because it gives the evolving drone roster and equipment systems a stronger sense of purpose. Skirmish play is useful for players primarily interested in the tactical mechanics without committing themselves as heavily to structured progression. However, the limited number of scenarios also reveals the game's modest scale. Anyone expecting the breadth of a large-budget strategy title, an enormous selection of battlefields, or an extensive narrative campaign should adjust expectations accordingly.

An unusual strength is its local multiplayer component, which accommodates as many as four players and includes shared or split-screen functionality as well as support for Remote Play Together. Multiplayer gives the tactical formula a somewhat different personality because additional players can introduce unpredictability into situations that are more controlled during solo play. It is a worthwhile extra feature, particularly for a smaller strategy game, and helps broaden the experience beyond its single-player campaign and skirmish content.

Presentation is functional rather than spectacular. Band of Drones does not rely on cinematic sequences or highly elaborate visual effects to create its appeal. Instead, the science-fiction setting serves the mechanics effectively, making upgrades, interchangeable weapons, modifications, and specialized mechanical units feel appropriate. The emphasis remains firmly on systems rather than characterization or dramatic storytelling. Players who mainly enjoy tactical planning may appreciate this direct approach, whereas those expecting rich characters, extensive lore, or a highly cinematic campaign may find the experience comparatively sparse.

Steam Deck compatibility is less straightforward. The game does not have an official Steam Deck compatibility rating indicating that it is Verified or Playable. Because of that, it should be regarded as officially unverified for Steam Deck rather than assumed to provide a fully optimized handheld experience. Its PC-oriented interface, controls, and older technical foundation may require manual configuration or experimentation when attempting to play it on the Deck. Players specifically purchasing it for handheld use should therefore keep this uncertainty in mind.

Overall, Band of Drones is an interesting small-scale tactical game whose strongest qualities come from the interaction between squad selection, unit progression, weapon customization, and varied mission objectives. Restricting deployments to six drones from a larger twelve-unit roster creates useful strategic decisions, while experience and equipment upgrades provide reasons to remain invested in individual machines. The limited scenarios and modest production values prevent it from competing with much larger tactical strategy games in sheer scope, but the underlying systems provide enough flexibility to make its battles engaging for players who enjoy methodical squad management. Local multiplayer is another welcome advantage that gives the package an extra dimension. It is ultimately best suited to strategy enthusiasts comfortable with a smaller indie experience and willing to overlook limited presentation in favor of customization and tactical decision-making.

Rating: 6/10
